assessment.thresholds: strong flare = X-class or M5+; strong geomagnetic storm = Kp >= 7
assessment.summary: Confirmed strong flare (X2.7); geomagnetic response max Kp 6.33 is below the Kp >= 7 threshold. Call it a strong solar flare, not a strong geomagnetic storm.

meta.note: Real NASA DONKI events. Show the event date and a DONKI link in-game; do not present snapshots as live data. strongFlare means an X-class or M5+ flare; strongGeomagneticStorm means Kp >= 7. A strong flare alone does not prove a strong geomagnetic storm, and Kp is Earth's geomagnetic index, not a Mars measurement. Use meta.assessment to choose wording.

CME first seen in the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-16T10:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a minor eruption seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 304 along with field line opening seen in SDO AIA 171, 193 and 211.

Very minor CME/jet first seen in the southeast by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-16T08:24Z, and possibly seen in one timestamp of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery. The source of this event may be a very faint dimming/post-eruptive arcades at around (N25E50) prior to 2025-05-16T08:00Z, best seen in SDO AIA 211.

CME first visible to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-05-16T04:28Z. CME is also faintly visible in SOHO LASCO C3 and in GOES CORR-1 but is not visible in STEREO A COR2. The beginning of this CME is covered by short data gaps in both SOHO LACSO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, so the actual start time is likely a few frames earlier. CME first seen in the NNE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2025-05-15T21:28Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR in later frames. This event only visible in later frames of STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 2025-05-25T19:53Z to 2025-05-18T01:53Z. The source of this event is a filament eruption from AR 4087 (N15W42) following an M2.1 class flare which resulted in associated CME: 2025-05-15T1

CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2025-05-15T20:24Z. CME is also visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Also faintly visible for a single frame in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is possibly the more southern portion of some ejecta from a small filament eruption from AR 14087 (N14E40-50) best seen in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2025-05-15T18:30Z.

Faint CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2. It is unclear if this CME is also visible in STEREO A COR2 due to data quality as well as GOES CCOR-1 due to obstruction from the control arm. The source appears to be an M2.1 flare from AR 14087 with associated filament ejecta best seen in SDO/AIA 304 and 131.
Faint, narrow CME to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is unclear, but may be associated with minor activity from AR 14087 in the NE.

Diffuse, fast CME front observed to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. The source is observed approximately around S34E80, as a small filament eruption in SDO AIA 304 and field line movement/small post-eruptive arcade in SDO AIA 171/193, beginning around 2025-05-15T02:45Z.

CME observed to the south in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and southwest in STEREO A COR2. The source is best observed in SDO AIA 304 and GOES SUVI 304 as filament ejecta peeking over the SW limb starting around 2025-05-15T01:09Z, and field line movement in SDO AIA 171/193 as early as 2025-05-15T00:21Z.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and is visible for one frame in STEREO A COR2 imagery prior to a data gap starting at 2025-05-14T18:53Z. The source is associated with the M4.7 flare and eruption from Active Region 14087 (N18E60) starting around 2025-05-14T18:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery.

Faint CME observed to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and about 4 frames at the edge of STEREO A COR2's field-of-view after a brief data gap from 2025-05-14T12:23Z-T15:53Z. The source may be field line movement over the southwest limb observed starting around 2025-05-14T15:15Z in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is associated with an M7.7 flare and eruption from Active Region 14087 (N16E62) starting around 2025-05-14T11:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is related to the X2.7 flare and eruption from Active Region 14087 (N16E64) starting around 2025-05-14T08:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 coronagraph imagery. The source is related to an M1.2 flare and eruption from Active Region 14087 (N17E88) starting around 2025-05-14T07:42Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. This event is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely related to an opening of field lines observed over the northwest limb starting around 2025-05-14T06:40Z as seen in SDO AIA 171,193 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery. This event overlaps with CME: 2025-05-14T06:24Z.

This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery for a few frames before overlapping CME: 2025-05-14T07:12Z overtakes this event. The source is likely far-sided and related to an opening of field lines observed over the northwest limb starting around 2025-05-14T06:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 171,193 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs. This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs. The source is likely an eruption observed just beyond the northeast limb starting around 2025-05-14T01:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines can be observed over the northeast limb at this time in SDO AIA 171 and 193 imagery as well.
